title: Stoplight Alternative: A Better Way to Manage API and Product Documentation
summary: Compare Stoplight and Theneo for API documentation, product guides, review workflows, and AI automation. Learn how Elva adds API discovery, governance, and MCP.
body_markdown:
Stoplight is a well-established platform for API design, documentation, and governance. Its visual OpenAPI editor, mocking capabilities, and specification validation make it a strong choice for design-first development teams.


But documentation needs have evolved. Teams aren't just documenting endpoints. They're building product guides, onboarding experiences, developer portals, and knowledge bases that need to stay accurate as products change.


They also need better ways to collaborate, review changes, automate updates, and make documentation accessible to AI tools and agents.


**[Theneo](https://www.theneo.io/) offers a Stoplight alternative for teams looking to manage more than API specifications.** It combines AI-powered documentation, product guides, advanced review workflows, and automation in one platform.


With[Elva](https://getelva.ai/) , the ecosystem extends into API discovery, design assistance, governance, testing, and AI-agent infrastructure.


‍


## Stoplight vs. Theneo: What's the Difference?


**Stoplight helps teams design and govern APIs. Theneo helps teams create, maintain, and publish documentation for APIs and products, with automation and AI-ready experiences built in.**


Capability Stoplight Theneo + Elva


Main focus API design Docs + API lifecycle


API references OpenAPI + guides AI-assisted, multi-format


Product guides Markdown guides Guides, onboarding, help


Automation Git workflows AI updates + CI/CD


Review process Discussions + Git Comments + approvals


AI and governance Spectral + mocking Elva catalog + MCP


For teams focused on designing APIs before development, Stoplight remains a strong option. For organizations looking to manage the entire documentation experience, Theneo offers a broader approach.


‍


## Beyond API References: Product Guides, Tutorials, and Onboarding


Documentation isn't just about explaining API endpoints. It's how users learn a product, complete their first integration, and troubleshoot problems.


Theneo brings different types of documentation into one platform:


- **API references** with interactive endpoints, schemas, and examples.
- **Getting-started guides** for developer and customer onboarding.
- **Product documentation** explaining features, configuration, and workflows.
- **Tutorials and integration guides** with step-by-step instructions.
- **Help centers and knowledge bases** for self-service support.
- **Changelogs and release notes** for communicating updates.


Teams can organize all these resources in a single branded portal.


Developers can work through Git, Markdown, and the CLI, while technical writers, product managers, and DevRel teams use the visual editor.


‍


## AI-Powered Documentation and Automated Updates


Keeping documentation current can take more effort than creating it.


Theneo helps reduce manual maintenance with AI-assisted writing, automatic API documentation generation, and integrations with development workflows.


Teams can generate endpoint descriptions, parameter explanations, and examples, improve existing content with AI, and synchronize documentation through Git and CI/CD pipelines.


The Theneo Agent can also identify code changes and propose documentation updates for review, while automated changelogs help communicate API changes and potential breaking changes.


Instead of treating documentation as a separate task after every release, teams can make it part of their development workflow.


‍


## Collaboration, Review, and Approval Workflows


Documentation often involves engineers, product managers, technical writers, DevRel, and security teams.


Theneo supports collaborative editing and[structured documentation review workflows](https://docs.theneo.io/the-editor/documentation-review) that help teams maintain quality before publishing.


Enterprise teams can:


- Create branches to prepare documentation changes.
- Leave inline comments and resolve feedback.
- Assign reviewers and approvers.
- Configure merge rules and required approvals.
- Review changes before merging them into published documentation.


These workflows apply to product guides, tutorials, API references, and other documentation content, without requiring every contributor to work through Git.


‍


## Developer Portals Built for Humans and AI Agents


Modern developer portals need to work for both human developers and AI-powered tools.


Theneo combines customizable documentation portals with AI-focused capabilities:


- **Ask AI:** Conversational answers based on published documentation.
- **llms.txt and llms-full.txt:** Structured resources for compatible AI tools.
- **MCP generation:** Expose API operations as tools for compatible AI agents.
- **Flexible portals:** Branded experiences combining guides, API references, changelogs, and private documentation.


These capabilities help developers find answers faster while making documentation more accessible to AI coding assistants and other supported tools.


For organizations that need hosted MCP servers with authorization and monitoring, Elva provides an additional management layer.


‍


## API Discovery, Design, and Governance with Elva


While Theneo focuses on documentation, **[Elva](https://getelva.ai/) extends the ecosystem into API discovery, governance, testing, and AI-agent infrastructure.**


Elva addresses a challenge that traditional design-first tools don't always solve: managing APIs that already exist, including those without complete specifications.


Its capabilities include:


- **[API discovery and cataloging](https://getelva.ai/catalog) :** Discover endpoints directly from repositories, generate OpenAPI specifications, organize collections, and assess API quality.
- **[API design and specification editing](https://app.getelva.ai/editor) :** Edit OpenAPI specifications with AI assistance and improve descriptions, schemas, and API design quality.
- **[API governance and contracts](https://getelva.ai/contracts) :** Define consumer-specific API contracts, detect breaking changes, and control what different audiences can access.
- **[Automated API testing](https://getelva.ai/testing) :** Generate contract tests, run CI checks, and validate API behavior before publishing changes.
- **[Managed MCP servers](https://getelva.ai/mcp) :** Generate and host MCP tools with authorization, scoped access, and activity monitoring.


Stoplight remains particularly strong for visual, design-first API development and mocking. Elva complements Theneo by addressing the ongoing management of APIs, from discovery and quality assessment to governance and controlled publishing.


**Together, Theneo and Elva connect documentation with API management.** Theneo helps teams document products and APIs, automate maintenance, and make documentation AI-ready. Elva helps them discover, design, govern, test, and expose APIs to developers and AI agents.


‍


## How to Migrate from Stoplight


Moving from Stoplight doesn't have to mean rebuilding your documentation manually.


Theneo's AI-powered CLI migration workflow helps transfer existing API references, product guides, Markdown content, and other accessible documentation.


After installing the latest CLI and making your documentation accessible to your AI coding agent, run:


` theneo migrate`


The agent-assisted workflow helps transfer content, organize pages, preserve important links, and validate the migration before publishing.


[Follow the step-by-step migration guide](https://docs.theneo.io/get-started/migrate-to-theneo) .


For larger projects, the Theneo team can assist with content migration, portal configuration, and integrations.


[Get migration assistance](https://www.theneo.io/book-demo) .


‍


## Which Documentation Platform Should You Choose?


**Choose Stoplight** if your main priorities are visual API design, specification governance, and mocking APIs before implementation.


**Choose Theneo** if you need AI-powered API documentation, product guides, onboarding tutorials, developer portals, advanced review workflows, and automated documentation maintenance.


**Choose Theneo with Elva** if you also need API discovery, design assistance, contract governance, automated testing, and managed AI-agent integrations.


Stoplight remains a strong API design platform. Theneo offers a broader approach to documentation that supports developers, product teams, technical writers, and AI-powered workflows.


With Elva, that experience extends into API management and agent-ready infrastructure.
